cues.text: A lunchbox feels heavy, while a bottle looks full. Are we measuring the same attribute? Imagine packing for a picnic. We need a balance for mass and a marked container for capacity. Let us choose useful units before measuring.

cues.asr_text: SUCCESS CRITERIA I CAN DISTINGUISH MASS FROM CAPACITY I CAN READ EQUAL SCALE INTERVALS I CAN COMBINE KILOGRAMS AND GRAMS OLETUS AND MILITAS

board_events.text: 3. Combine kilograms and grams or litres and millilitres.

cues.text: Mass describes how heavy an object is; capacity describes how much a container can hold. Use grams or kilograms for mass, and millilitres or litres for capacity. One kilogram is one thousand grams. One litre is one thousand millilitres. On every scale, count equal intervals before deciding what one interval represents.
cues.asr_text: MUST DESCRIBES HOW HEAVY AN OBJECT IS CAPACITY DESCRIBES HOW MUCH A CONTAINER CAN HOLD USE CRAMS OR KILOGRAMS FOR MASS AND MILITORS OR LITRES FOR CAPACITY ONE KILOGRAM IS ONE THOUSAND GRAMS ONE LITRE IS ONE THOUSAND MILLETRES ON EVERY SCALE COUNT EQUAL INTERVALS BEFORE DECIDING WHAT ONE INTERVAL REPRESENTS

cues.text: A bag has a mass of one kilogram and three hundred and fifty grams. Picture one thousand grams as a whole kilogram, with the smaller amount added alongside. What single gram reading would describe the same mass?
cues.asr_text: A BAG HAS A MASS OF ONE KILOGRAM AND THREE HUNDRED AND FIFTY GRAMS PICTURE ONE THOUSAND GRAMS AS A WHOLE KILOGRAM WITH THE SMALLER AMOUNT ADDED ALONGSIDE WHAT SINGLE GRAM READING WOULD DESCRIBE THE SAME MASS

cues.text: One thousand plus three hundred and fifty is one thousand three hundred and fifty grams. The bag has not become heavier because we changed its name. Kilograms and grams are two units for the same attribute.
cues.asr_text: ONE THOUSAND PLUS THREE HUNDRED AND FIFTY IS ONE THOUSAND THREE HUNDRED AND FIFTY GRAMS THE BAG HAS NOT BECOME HEAVIER BECAUSE WE CHANGED ITS NAME KILOGRAMS AND GRAMS ARE TWO UNITS FOR THE SAME ATTRIBUTE

cues.text: A jug holds two litres and two hundred and fifty millilitres. Convert the whole litres first. Two groups of one thousand millilitres make two thousand millilitres. Then include the extra marked amount.
cues.asr_text: A JUG HOLDS TWO LEATERS AND TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY MILLETRES CONVERT THE WHOLE LEADERS FIRST TWO GROUPS OF ONE THOUSAND MILLETRES MAKE TWO THOUSAND MILLETRES THEN INCLUDE THE EXTRA MARKED AMOUNT

cues.text: The capacity is two thousand two hundred and fifty millilitres. On a scale from zero to one thousand with four equal intervals, each interval would be two hundred and fifty millilitres. Count intervals, not just tick marks.
cues.asr_text: THE CAPACITY IS TWO THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY MILLETRES ON A SCALE FROM ZERO TO ONE THOUSAND WITH FOUR EQUAL INTERVALS EACH INTERVAL WOULD BE TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY MILLETRES COUNT INTERVALS NOT JUST TAKE MARKS

cues.text: Grams and millilitres are not interchangeable labels. A balance measures mass; a marked jug measures capacity. Equal numerical readings do not make those attributes the same. Read the instrument and include the correct unit.
cues.chapter: Match the unit to the attribute
cues.asr_text: GRAMS AND MILILEATORS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE LABELS A BALANCE MEASURES MASS A MARKED JUG MEASURES CAPACITY EQUAL NUMERICAL READINGS DO NOT MAKE THOSE ATTRIBUTES THE SAME READ THE INSTRUMENT AND INCLUDE THE CORRECT UNIT

cues.text: A balance points halfway between five hundred and six hundred grams. What mass does it show? Look at the model, and keep your prediction in mind.
cues.asr_text: A BALANCE POINTS HALFWAY BETWEEN FIVE HUNDRED AND SIX HUNDRED GRAMS WHAT MASS DOES IT SHOW LOOK AT THE MODEL AND KEEP YOUR PREDICTION IN MIND

cues.text: Halfway is fifty grams beyond five hundred, giving five hundred and fifty grams. The scale is measuring mass, so the answer needs grams, not millilitres.
cues.asr_text: HALF WAY IS FIFTY GRAMS BEYOND FIVE HUNDRED GIVING FIVE HUNDRED AND FIFTY GRAMS THE SCALE IS MEASURING MASS SO THE ANSWER NEEDS GRAMS NOT MILILETAS
